description: S11 acceptance input: one noisy webcam gaze stream, hand-written to exercise every
stage of web/src/capture/FixationFilter.ts. `expected_fixations.json` is the
hand-derived output and carries the arithmetic.
Timestamps are a clean 20 ms cadence (50 Hz) so the derivation is checkable by eye;
real WebGazer samples arrive at roughly 30 Hz with fractional performance.now() stamps.
Coordinates are CSS pixels on a 1280x800 screen.
What is deliberately in here:
- fixation A at (500,300), a period-3 sawtooth of +-4 px that a median-5 filter
annihilates, so the jitter must not survive into the centroid;
- one single-sample spike (t=1080, 700,100) at FULL confidence: only the median
filter can remove it, the confidence gate cannot;
- one low-confidence wild sample inside fixation A (t=1120, conf 0.30) which must be
dropped BEFORE the median filter, and whose removal leaves a 40 ms gap in the
stream that must not split the fixation;
- a two-sample saccade (t=1220, t=1240) that belongs to no fixation;
- a 60 ms cluster at (900,420) - a real pause, but under the 100 ms minimum, so it
must yield nothing;
- a three-sample low-confidence burst (t=1340..1380, conf 0.45/0.25/0.10) sitting
between two fixations: keeping any of them would change the answer;
- fixation B at (300,500) drifting to (340,516). Its dispersion peaks at exactly
40 + 16 = 56 px, inside the 60 px threshold, so the drift stays one fixation and
its centroid is a real mean that equals no individual sample;
- fixation C at (700,200), spanning exactly 100 ms and running to the end of the
stream, so it can only be emitted by end().
